latest_release.body:
> [!TIP]
> Termix is free and always will be. If it's useful to you, consider [donating](https://donate.termix.site/donate/) to support development.

### Added

- What plugins add to the app is kept on the server too, so a new browser, device or cleared cache opens almost as fast as usual instead of starting every plugin first
- The first time plugins have to start one by one, one screen says so with how far along it is, instead of a page that keeps changing
- Plugin pages can let Termix scroll them, so parts from other plugins on the page move with it instead of trailing behind
- Plugin pages can tell when parts from other plugins on them have drawn, so they can show one loading screen instead of filling in piece by piece
- Secret references like `bw://web-1/username` also work in a host's or credential's username, and in the username of other protocol logins
- Desktop app: closing the window can quit Termix instead of keeping it in the tray
- Desktop app: the first time closing the window keeps Termix in the tray, a notice says it is still running and how to quit
- Admin setting to trust a host's first key without a prompt when nobody can confirm it. Each such key is audited
- Every desktop file, tarball and Flatpak bundle on a release carries signed build provenance, and each release has a signed `SHA256SUMS` file with build provenance in `SHA256SUMS.intoto.jsonl`. Check them with the new Verify your download page in the docs
- Docker images are signed with cosign and carry build provenance and an SBOM attestation
- Desktop app: Windows builds are code signed, thanks to Ember Swan
- A CycloneDX SBOM of the server's dependencies ships with each build: `/app/sbom.cdx.json` in the Docker image and `termix_sbom.cdx.json` on the release
- The server sends the same security headers with or without the bundled nginx: a strict Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and HSTS over HTTPS
- Desktop app: the app page carries a Content-Security-Policy
- Limits on how often logins, second factor checks, password resets, sign ups, API key creation, exports and imports can be tried, per address and per account. Too many bad API keys from one address are refused for a while
- Rotate the encryption key from the API (`POST /encryption/rotate-key`) or with `ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS`, and the database key with `DATABASE_KEY_PREVIOUS`. Everything moves to the new key at start
- The example Docker compose drops every capability it doesn't need, sets no-new-privileges and shows a read-only, non-root setup. The image runs on a read-only root filesystem
- Every plugin made for plugin API 2 runs in its own process. It can only read its own files, opens no network connections or programs unless it was granted that, and reaches Termix only through checked calls. Secrets, the database, SSH connections and saved logins stay in the server
- The desktop app fences each plugin the same way: it runs on its own copy of Node inside the system's sandbox (an AppContainer on Windows, a Seatbelt profile on macOS, Landlock and seccomp on Linux), so it can't read your files or the database, start programs or open connections it wasn't granted, and it is stopped when it goes over its memory limit.
- Desktop app: plugin frames keep the frame rules the server sends
- In the Docker image each plugin also runs as its own Linux user, so it can't read the database, keys or other plugins' data. With `NET_ADMIN`, plugins that may not open connections are also blocked by a firewall rule
- The screens of every plugin made for plugin API 2 run in sandboxed frames with no access to your login, the rest of the page or other plugins. Each frame reaches only its own plugin, with a short key that ends with your session, and asks Termix for anything else through a fixed list of checks. They keep the same look, theme, shortcuts and language. A frame loads nothing from other sites: pictures come through Termix, and it can only cover the s

detail.readme:
Termix

Self-hosted, plugin-based server management


## Overview Termix is a free, open source, self-hosted server management platform built on plugins. The core keeps your hosts, credentials, users, sharing and sessions. Everything else, like the SSH terminal, remote desktop, file manager, Docker and metrics, is a plugin you can turn on, off or remove. It runs on web, desktop and mobile. Think of it as a free, self-hosted Termius.
## Try the Demo Try it at [demo.termix.site](https://demo.termix.site/). Any username and password works.
## Core What every install has, with or without plugins: - Hosts: Save hosts in nested folders with tags and parent hosts, bulk edit, import and export, and use Quick Connect for one-off connections - Credentials: Reuse saved passwords and keys across hosts, with host defaults you can set for the server, a user or a folder - Sharing and Roles: Share hosts, credentials and folders with users or roles at four levels: connect, view, edit and manage - Accounts: Local accounts, sessions you can see and revoke, trusted devices, API keys and an audit log - Security: Passwords, keys and other secrets are encrypted per user, and the database can be encrypted on disk - Desktop Sync: The desktop app runs on its own and can link to a Termix server to keep an offline copy of your account - Interface: Tabs and split screen, a command palette (double tap left shift), rebindable shortcuts, themes, branding and around 30 languages - Databases: SQLite by default, with PostgreSQL and MySQL supported too
## Plugins Plugins add everything else. Admins can install, update or remove plugins from the Plugins tab, and each plugin has its own repo. These ship in the default image: | Plugin | What it does | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | [Alerts](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-Alerts) | icon rail, sidebar, tab bar and dock. | | [Classic Themes](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-Classic-Themes) | Light, dark and seven more color themes for Termix. | | [Credential Tools](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-Credential-Tools) | Generate SSH keys, check them and copy a public key to a host. | | [Docker](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-Docker) | Manage Docker and Podman containers on your hosts over SSH, with logs, stats and a console. | | [File Manager](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-File-Manager) | Browse, edit and move files over SFTP, including All other official plugins (55) These ship in the `-full` image tags (like `latest-full`) and the full desktop builds. Want to build your own? Start from the [plugin template](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix-Plugin-Template). Plugins you can install are listed in the [registry](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix-Registry). Turn on the community registry in Plugins, Registries to install plugins made by other people, or add your own registry. See [submitting a plugin](https://docs.termix.site/develop/community-registry) and [hosting your own registry](https://docs.termix.site/develop/registries#host-your-own-registry).
## Platform Support
Platform Distribution
Web Any modern browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) | PWA support
Windows x64/arm64 Portable | EXE and MSI Installer | Full EXE (all plugins) | Chocolatey
Linux x64/arm64 Portable | AUR | AppImage | Deb | Full AppImage and Deb (all plugins) | Flatpak
macOS Universal/x64/arm64, v12.0+ Apple App Store | DMG | Full DMG (all plugins) | Homebrew
iOS/iPadOS v15.1+ Apple App Store | IPA
Android v7.0+ Google Play Store | APK

## Installation See the [docs](https://docs.termix.site/install) for install steps on every platform. On macOS, Termix, Menu Bar Icon picks a monochrome icon (the default), a color icon or no icon. The choice is saved on this device. With the icon hidden, open Termix from the Dock to change it back, and closing the last window quits the app. Sample Docker Compose file. Remote desktop (RDP, VNC and Telnet) is built in, so nothing else needs to run next to it: ```yaml services: termix: image: ghcr.io/termix-ssh/termix:latest container_name: termix restart: unless-stopped ports: - "8080:8080" volumes: - termix-data:/app/data environment: PORT: "8080" volumes: termix-data: driver: local ``` ### Cloud Hosting If Termix runs on the network it manages, an outage takes it down right when you need it. A VPS keeps it reachable, gives you a static IP and works from anywhere without a VPN or port forward. [GINERNET](https://docs.termix.site/install/ginernet) sponsors Termix and the docs have a setup guide for their VPS.
## Donate Termix has no paid plans. Donations cover servers, domains and development time. [Donate](https://donate.termix.site/)
## Sponsors For a paid sponsor spot, email [mail@termix.site](mailto:mail@termix.site).

                           

## Support Bugs and ideas for Termix itself (login, hosts, credentials, sharing, sync, the app and desktop app) go in this repo: [report a bug](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) or [request a feature](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml). Every plugin has its own repo, so a problem with the terminal, file manager, Docker, remote desktop or any other plugin goes in that plugin's repo (see the table above, or use Report an issue on the plugin's page in the app, which fills in your versions for you). Not sure where it goes? Open it here and it will be moved. You need a GitHub account. Add as much detail as you can, in English if possible. For discussions and questions, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jVQGdvHDrf) server. Update videos are on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@TermixSSH/videos).
